done.why: I died for the third time, crushed when I grabbed the crown in the Dusty Room after blowing open the safe. The face in the black mist gave up on me, the score came up (115 of 400, Novice Adventurer), and the world went dark for good. There was nothing left to do.

about: The Wizard's leftovers from the Great Underground Empire. A doddering wizard stole the Empire's treasures, scattered them through the caverns south of the ravine, and keeps popping in to cast spells starting with F at you. I was trying to get the loot back: answer a stone door's riddle, ride a bucket up a well, outwit the Bank of Zork's walls of light, trick a dragon into melting a glacier, fly a balloon up a volcano, and blow open a safe. It's a chain of old-school object puzzles, and the world gives just enough hints to keep you moving.

ending.what: Game over. On my third death (the ceiling fell in the Dusty Room after I took the crown) the face refused to bring me back. Final score 115 of 400, Novice Adventurer, in 291 moves.

moments.note: The Wizard's first visit actually tells me what I'm here for: treasures south of the ravine, pearls behind a door that asks a question, a room that won't keep still. It gave me a goal right away.
The yellow sphere was a Wizard illusion. The room 'has the grace to look embarrassed about it'. Charming.
The carousel room's spinning floor gets explained in-world, along with a hint that someone could find the works and stop it.
In the oddly-angled maze, 'There is no way to go in that direction' printed and then a room description came anyway. I couldn't tell whether I'd moved.
Answering 'a well' got a hollow laugh. 'say well' worked. The article mattered.
Thunderclap, and the stone door swings open.
Examining the bucket basically walks you through the water-and-teapot solution, and does it nicely.
The random carousel turned every trip into a slot machine. It took many tries each time to land where I wanted.
I ate the green cake without carrying the red one, so I was shrunk with the red cake out of reach on the giant table. I realized I'd stranded the pool puzzle.
I dove into the pool and drowned. The resurrection by the face in the mist was a nice touch, but all my things were scattered.
I cracked the bank. Going out a teller doorway and back in, then through the curtain with the loot, put me in the West Viewing Room, and from there I could walk out.
The Wizard whispered an F-word and both bank treasures vanished from my hands right after I'd worked so hard for them.
The dragon followed me twice and then lost interest at the Cool Room. Kicking didn't keep him angry enough.
Kicked the dragon one time too many and got incinerated.
My scattered belongings had all ended up in the gazebo. Great relief.
The dragon sees his reflection in the glacier, breathes fire, drowns in the meltwater. Great payoff, with a moby ruby behind it.
Balloon flight with the newspaper as fuel, then LAND on the ledge. It felt like real progress.
Took the crown and 5000 tons of rock fell on me. That was my last life. A sudden and final ending.

wished: I wished I could tell where the scattered things went after a death without hunting for them (they turned out to be in the gazebo, which was lucky).
I wished the carousel could be stopped. Some 'works' were hinted at, but I never found them, and getting anywhere was a dice roll.
I wished 'answer a well' had been accepted like 'say well'.
I wished I'd been warned more clearly that the Dusty Room walls would come down if I lingered. 'The walls seem ready to collapse' came one line before I died, and I had no lives left.
I wished I could keep the bank treasures. The Wizard took them right after I got them out.
I wished I could get the red cake down after shrinking, to try the pool properly.

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you; the pearls nearest, behind a stone door that asks a question, and the rest further in, past a room that will not keep still.
lines.why: This gave me my purpose and a rough map. It's exactly what a goal-seeker wants.

lines.line: It was never there: the Wizard's word put it in the room, and the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: Funny, and it taught me the Wizard makes illusions.

lines.line: Whatever it is that makes it go up, it will go up with what is in it and without what is not; that is the whole art of buckets.
lines.why: A lovely hint for the well puzzle.

lines.line: It is the doorway that bars it, not the room: the Bank built its doorways to know its own property going through them, and whatever you are carrying, they know. The curtain of light was not built by the same people.
lines.why: This is what pointed me at the curtain to solve the bank.

lines.line: Dragons are smart, but sometimes naive, and this one has never seen ice before.
lines.why: The best payoff of the session.

lines.line: "Not you again! This is getting tedious. You'll obviously never be much help to me. Better luck next time, oh wondrous adventurer."
lines.why: The final death, delivered with contempt.

fun.why: Solving the riddle door, the bank and the dragon was really satisfying, and the balloon was a joy. The randomized carousel and two avoidable deaths dragged it down.

engagement.why: I always knew what I was chasing: treasures, then the next locked thing. The hints kept pulling me forward, even after the Wizard robbed me at turn 170.

difficulty.why: It's hard and unforgiving. I stranded the pool puzzle with the cakes, lost my treasures to the Wizard, and died to the dragon and the collapsing room. Still, most puzzles were solvable from the in-world hints, so it felt fair, if harsh.

interestingness.why: Lots of different mechanisms: illusions, a spinning room, walls you walk through, a reflection-baited dragon, a hot-air balloon. Each puzzle felt like its own little machine.

prose.why: The dry, wry voice in the added descriptions (the embarrassed room, the art of buckets, the bank's doorways) is a pleasure. A few parser hiccups grated, like 'You must tell me how to do that to a purple book' at turn 267 and 'With a matchbook??!?' at turn 284.
